entries.title: Senate Advances Immigration Bill Without ‘Anti-Weaponization’ Fund and Ballroom Money
entries.summary: Republicans had held up the enforcement package amid concerns about the political fund.
entries.content:
Senate Republicans are moving ahead with a multibillion-dollar spending bill for immigration and border enforcement after the White House dropped plans for a controversial ‘anti-weaponization’ fund.

The Senate advanced the budget reconciliation legislation Wednesday, 53-46, in a party line vote. The chamber could consider dozens of amendments to the package on Thursday during a “vote-a-rama” with hopes of sending the legislation to the House by the end of this week.

Senate Republicans had previously blocked the legislation over concerns about President Donald Trump’s $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund, which was announced as part of his settlement with the IRS over leaked tax forms. Some senators who warned the fund could have been used to boost Trump allies wanted to impose guardrails on it as part of the bill.
entries.author: Avani Kalra

entries.title: House Votes to Limit Trump’s Iran War Powers
entries.summary: The vote is a rebuke to the president, who has insisted he doesn’t need congressional approval for action on Iran.
entries.content:
The House voted Wednesday to limit President Donald Trump’s war powers in a sign that the push to rein in the president has moved beyond Democratic protest votes.

The measure, introduced by Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-New York), passed 215-208 after failing in three previous votes.

Republican Reps. Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Tom Barrett of Michigan and Warren Davidson of Ohio joined Democrats in supporting the measure. Rep. Jared Golden of Maine, the only Democrat who previously voted against similar measures, flipped this time.
entries.author: Hamed Ahmadi
